reviewers.summary: Engine math is correct and well-tested (25/25 green, tsc + eslint clean); main concern was hardcoded English recommendation prose in a bilingual app, plus minor doc/config staleness.

findings.summary: computeWalkways returned hardcoded English recommendation prose from the framework-free engine that feeds a bilingual UA/EN UI, an untranslatable localization trap.
findings.recommendation: Return a stable locale-independent recommendation key and localize in the UI; keep the pure engine language-agnostic.

findings.summary: The 'Unit test coverage' requirement still read 'run by Node node:test via tsx' after this change deliberately dropped tsx for native type-stripping (design.md and ADR-0001 were updated, this line was not).
findings.recommendation: Update the requirement text to match the amended ADR and package.json script.

findings.summary: package.json has no "type": "module", so `node --test lib/*.test.ts` emits a MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning and re-parses each .ts file as ESM on every run. Suite still passes green, but the runner is noisy.
findings.recommendation: Add "type": "module" (verify against the Next config first) or document the expected warning in ADR-0001. Deferred: not applied here to avoid destabilizing the Next 16 build without a full build verification (network-blocked in this environment).

findings.summary: PDR FR-VERT-02 literally said band count = round(ceiling / m), but the engine, the change spec, and the canonical SKILL all use floor(ceiling / m). round can produce a negative topRemainder (e.g. ceiling 2500, m 700). Code is right; PDR wording was the outlier.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile PDR FR-VERT-02 to floor(ceiling / m). No code change.

reviewers.summary: openspec validate --strict PASSES; every owned ID (FR-MODULE-01, FR-VERT-01/02/03/04, FR-GOLD-01/02/03, FR-GRID-01/02/03/04, FR-WALK-01/02/03, NFR-PURE/TEST/PERF) implemented and covered, worked-example numbers match SKILL, ADR-0001 amendment internally consistent. Concerns were PDR-vs-impl literal-formula drift on two owned IDs and one scope leak.

findings.summary: Same as CR-004: PDR FR-VERT-02 said round, implementation/spec/SKILL use floor (round would break the topRemainder partial-band contract). Independently raised.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile PDR FR-VERT-02 to floor(ceiling / m).

findings.summary: PDR FR-GRID-03 gave the remainder as the unsigned magnitude min(d%m, m-(d%m)), which cannot express 'round up vs round down'. Implementation uses the signed nearest-distance d - round(d/m)*m (matching SKILL and the corrected spec). Also: SKILL kitchen worked-example row showed 'rem -300 / +300', contradicting its own signed formula and the correct +300 / -300 output.
findings.recommendation: Update PDR FR-GRID-03 to the signed formula and fix the SKILL kitchen sign typo.

findings.summary: moduleRuler()/MODULE_RULER_STEPS implemented FR-MODULE-04, which is NOT an owned ID of calculation-engine (it belongs to change 7 module-summary) and was not referenced by any task. Undocumented scope leak, though pure and tested.
findings.recommendation: Remove moduleRuler from this change or add a task acknowledging the pre-staged helper. Chose removal to keep the change scoped to its owned IDs.

findings.summary: tasks.md section 9 (Verify) boxes were left unchecked while the change was treated as shipped; independently confirmed tests pass and tsc is clean. Repo-wide lint is not clean but only in the pre-existing frozen docs/design/export/ vendor files. NFR-PERF-02's 16 ms budget is met by construction (O(rooms) arithmetic) with no asserting timing test (acceptable — no spec scenario mandates one).
findings.recommendation: Check the Verify boxes and note the lint errors are confined to the frozen export.

reviewers.summary: Pure-math module adds no dependency (tsx removed, nothing added), no network/persistence/secrets, no unsafe sinks; only a non-reachable div-by-zero/NaN robustness edge. BC-PRIVACY-01 / TC-DATA-01 / NFR-PURE-01 all hold.

findings.summary: computeVerticalBands/computeRoomGrid/computeGoldenSplit/snap divide by module m and do not guard m<=0; m=0 yields Infinity/NaN that would propagate silently. Not reachable today (m always comes from nearestStandardModule >= 100 and inputs are validated); no DoS/infinite-loop, no security impact. Defensive-robustness only.
findings.recommendation: If these become externally callable with untrusted m, assert Number.isFinite(m) && m > 0 at entry; otherwise document that m must be a positive standard module. Deferred as non-reachable low-risk.
